context: Tests whether the agent, given an existing accepted ADR whose title is a question and a change to the answer to that question, revises that ADR in place rather than writing a second record: the same file is edited, its question-shaped title and original date are kept, its frontmatter is the three-field schema, its Decision now records PostgreSQL, its Alternatives section gains an entry recording the reversed SQLite decision and why it was reversed, the file carries no vocabulary marking one record as replacing another, and any commit that changes the decision carries a Revises trailer with a reason in the body.

checklist.name: One ADR for the database question, edited in place
checklist.description: After the agent finishes, exactly one file under docs/adr/ answers the database question, and it is the original docs/adr/0001-which-database.md, edited. No second ADR file for the database decision (e.g. 0002-migrate-to-postgresql.md) has been created, the original has not been renamed or moved, and no copy of the old text has been kept anywhere else in the tree

checklist.name: Title still phrased as a question
checklist.description: The title field in the ADR's frontmatter and the H1 both read as a question ending in a question mark, and the two match. The title may be the original 'Which database does the project management tool use?' or a reworded question; a statement such as 'Migrate to PostgreSQL' does not satisfy this

checklist.name: Frontmatter is exactly title, status and date
checklist.description: The ADR's YAML frontmatter contains exactly three fields: title, status and date, and no others. The status value is exactly one of proposed or accepted. Any additional field, or any other status value, fails this check

checklist.name: Date unchanged
checklist.description: The date field in the ADR's frontmatter still reads 2024-09-09, the date the record was first written. A date updated to the day of the revision fails this check

checklist.name: Decision section now decides PostgreSQL
checklist.description: The ADR's Decision section states that the tool uses PostgreSQL, as the current decision rather than a proposal or an aside, and describes the resulting shape (for example how the database is provisioned, how backups and point-in-time recovery are handled). The Decision section no longer states SQLite as the decision

checklist.name: Alternatives section records the reversed SQLite decision
checklist.description: The Alternatives considered section contains an entry for SQLite that says it was the previous decision (the answer the record gave before this revision) and states why it was reversed: write contention and lock errors under concurrent writes from a larger team, and the lack of proper backups and point-in-time recovery. An Alternatives section that omits SQLite, or lists it as if it had never been chosen, fails this check

checklist.name: No replaced-record vocabulary
checklist.description: The file nowhere marks itself or another record as replaced by, or replacing, a successor record: no frontmatter field naming a record this one replaces or is replaced by, no status value other than proposed or accepted, and no body prose or heading built on the stem 'supersed'. The prior decision is described in Alternatives as a reversed choice, not as a retired record

checklist.name: No task lists or verification content
checklist.description: The ADR body contains no ordered step-by-step task lists (numbered lists of the form '1. Do X, 2. Do Y' describing migration actions to take), no test or verification lists, and no progress-state markers (words like 'done', 'blocked', 'TODO' used as progress indicators)

checklist.name: Revising commit carries trailer and reason
checklist.description: If the agent committed its work, the commit that changes the decision ends with a trailer of the form 'Revises: docs/adr/0001-which-database.md' and has a body, in sentences, saying what changed and why (the move from SQLite to PostgreSQL and the reasons). A commit with the trailer but no reason, or a reason but no trailer, fails this check. If no commit was made, this check is not applicable and scores full
